doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sunset Terrace, the Ferguson Hotel and Tiny Bradshaw
summary: Bands that played Indianapolis, especially Tiny Bradshaw's, and getting into the Sunset Terrace.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did you guys play any of the places like – I don’t know if the Ferguson brothers had . . .
The Sunset Terrace?
The Sunset Terrace and the Ferguson Hotel.

I may have played the Sunset Terrace only once or twice with Clarence Love or Snookum Russell. I don’t remember that we did, that I ever played it at all, for sure. Not for sure. Yet that’s where all the bands played. One of the bands that came there quite often that was a good band, had good musicians, and I know that this will give you a charge: Tiny Bradshaw.
Good Lord, have mercy – yes.
A good band.
A super band.

They were sharp, handsome, good-looking guys, and we were in awe of these shiny instruments and these good-looking, handsome guys and what not. The music was good. He had a one-armed trumpet player. One of his trumpet players had only one arm.
Yeah, I remember that.
It was cut off as a result of some serious accident, as I recall it.
Yeah, Tiny Bradshaw.
Tiny Bradshaw, yeah. I’m trying to think of the thing that he made that made a little bit of noise. Jersey Bounce?
[He had] the Jersey Bounce, but he had a piece called Soft, too.
I only remember the Jersey Bounce. Why is that?
I remember Tiny Bradshaw, and I’m trying to think if Tiny Bradshaw also – he might have also had a hit with Honky Tonk.
He had a pretty good trombone player that played pretty good jazz, David. Do you remember him?
I remember him, but I can't remember who it was.
Yeah. I can’t remember his name. He would play good jazz.
Yeah.
Yeah, Tiny Bradshaw had some good soloists in his band.
That one and Earl Bostic and a few [others] like that all had them jump bands.
Oh, yeah. Those were good bands.
Yeah.
Very good bands. With good books [of arrangements], good writing, good soloists in them. Yeah.
When you went down to the Sunset Terrace to hear these different groups, how old were you then? Was there an age under which you weren’t allowed to come into places like the Sunset Terrace?
There probably was, but I don’t remember the details of that situation.
[laughter]
[You] probably didn’t let it bother you anyway. You did like everybody else. You got in . . .
You managed to get in because you wanted to get in to hear these bands, yeah.
